detail.title: Stagnant Income and Rising Vulnerability: An Assessment of Agricultural Households in the Period of Doubling Farmers' Income in India
detail.abstract: Vulnerability of agricultural households remains persistent, even after multiple policy initiatives in India. Using the Situation Assessment Survey of NSSO for the year 2012-13 and 2018-19, this paper sheds light on various forms of vulnerability faced by the agricultural households in India in the period of Doubling Farmers' Income initiative. Despite efforts, there is large scale prevalence of households with insufficient income to meet consumption expenditure, consequently increasing indebtedness. Moreover, the existing price policy, particularly concerning certain crops such as Minimum Support Price (MSP) falls short in alleviating vulnerability and thus warrants modification based on the recommendation of Swaminathan Committee.

title: Multi-Channel Composite Indicator for FX Portfolio Crises: Architecture, Evaluation, and the Limits of Small-Sample Calibration

detail.title: Multi-Channel Composite Indicator for FX Portfolio Crises: Architecture, Evaluation, and the Limits of Small-Sample Calibration
detail.abstract: This paper develops a Multi-Channel Composite Indicator (MCCI) for predicting FX portfolio crises using options-implied and geopolitical signals. The system constructs the MCCI from five channels, each targeting a distinct risk mechanism: geopolitical risk, tail-risk pricing, crash fear, market microstructure, and volatility divergence. Each channel is estimated via logistic regression with walk-forward validation, and the composite is formed by equal-weighted averaging of z-scored out-of-sample probabilities. The novel Volatility Divergence Index (VDX), which captures the implied-realized volatility spread as a crisis predictor rather than a volatility forecast, serves as the system's anchor signal and appears in all five channel models. Evaluated against expandingwindow crisis labels on a portfolio of nine G10 FX pairs over 2020-2025, the MCCI achieves strong discrimination (AUC 0.903 at the 90-day horizon, 0.769 at 30 days), significantly outperforming a naive CVIX benchmark at longer horizons (DeLong p < 0.001). However, with only three crisis episodes in the evaluation sample, probability calibration fails and no operationally useful alert threshold can be identified. Episode-level analysis reveals that aggregate discrimination is dominated by the 2020 COVID crisis, with substantially weaker performance during the 2022 rate shock and 2025 tariff episode. The comprehensive evaluation methodology itself constitutes a contribution, demonstrating that strong aggregate AUC can coexist with poor calibration and heterogeneous episode-level performance when crisis counts are small, and quantifying minimum data requirements for operational early warning deployment.

title: Automated Decision-Making and the Limits of Law Designed for Humans
affiliations: Curtin University - Curtin Law School

detail.title: Automated Decision-Making and the Limits of Law Designed for Humans
detail.abstract: In the broader discussions surrounding artificial intelligence, this article examines the extent to which Australian administrative law is equipped to accommodate automated and AIassisted decision-making in tax administration. While such technologies promise gains in efficiency and scale, the avenues for challenging tax assessments and related decisions remain narrowly circumscribed. Under Part IVC of the Taxation Administration Act 1953 (Cth), assessment-making is insulated from scrutiny by the combined statutory effect that an assessment is prima facie valid and that a notice of assessment constitutes conclusive evidence of its due making. Judicial review of assessment-making may be available under s 75(v) of the Constitution and its statutory counterparts in s 39B of the Judiciary Act 1903 (Cth), but these provisions are difficult to apply in the absence of an identifiable officer in the case of automated tax administration. Certain non-assessment decisions are reviewable under the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act 1977 (Cth), yet prevailing authority requires a reviewable decision to involve a human mental process. Private law remedies are available, but their applications are practically limited. The article argues that targeted legislative reform, strengthened transparency obligations and clearer attribution of responsibility are required to ensure the safeguarding of taxpayer rights in an increasingly automated tax administration environment.

title: Loss-Leader Pricing on Hybrid Platforms: A Multiproduct Perspective
affiliations: ,  and Graduate School of Business Administration, Kobe University

detail.title: Loss-Leader Pricing on Hybrid Platforms: A Multiproduct Perspective
detail.abstract: We develop a model of a hybrid platform that hosts multiple products and enables consumers to fill their baskets through one-stop shopping. Each product is supplied by a manufacturer and sold via competing third-party sellers, while the platform also enters as a first-party seller. One-stop shopping turns otherwise independent products into effective complements, creating a cross-product demand externality (the Cournot externality). We show that the platform may optimally price one product below cost (loss-leader pricing) to internalize this Cournot externality, particularly when manufacturers' wholesale prices are high. Ceteris paribus, loss-leader pricing benefits the platform, consumers, and manufacturers, yielding a Pareto improvement. However, this positive outcome may fail to arise---and indeed leave all parties worse off---when manufacturers strategically raise wholesale prices in anticipation of the platform's loss-leading. Our analysis finds that whenever loss-leading is profitable for the platform, it also benefits consumers and manufacturers, providing a procompetitive rationale for first-party selling by hybrid platforms.

title: The Quantum Blind Spot: A Fiduciary's Guide to Bitcoin's Existential Risk
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: The Quantum Blind Spot: A Fiduciary's Guide to Bitcoin's Existential Risk
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether quantum computing represents a material risk requiring attention from institutional investors holding Bitcoin allocations. Through analysis of recent technical developments, expert assessments, and governance structures, the research demonstrates that quantum computing poses a potential existential threat to Bitcoin's cryptographic foundation within a timeframe that now overlaps with the governance timeline required for implementing protective measures. Crucially, the study argues that this risk extends beyond direct on-chain ownership to include spot ETFs and corporate proxies; these instruments face a compounding "custodial-quantum" risk where centralized pools of assets are vulnerable to both underlying network failure and the potential inability of custodians to migrate vast holdings before a cryptographic breach. The analysis reveals that fiduciaries face an unprecedented challenge: responsibility for assets secured by software they cannot control, maintained by developers they cannot direct, and governed by a decentralized community resistant to institutional influence. The paper concludes with specific action items for investment committees, board trustees, and institutional fund managers to fulfill their fiduciary obligations considering this emerging risk.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether shifts in return-to-office (RTO) expectations were associated with differential return performance across commercial real estate sectors. We construct a panel of U.S. publicly traded equity REITs using historical constituent holdings of the Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ) and obtain daily adjusted price data from public market sources, including Yahoo Finance. The sample spans January 1, 2022 through January 1, 2025. We implement a quasi-experimental framework combining difference-indifferences estimation with a dynamic event-study design around January 3, 2023, RTO expectation shift. Office REITs are compared with Industrial, Data Center, and broader non-office REIT sectors. We find a positive and statistically significant post-event differential return for Office REITs, though the economic magnitude is modest. Event-study estimates indicate gradual relative performance adjustment rather than immediate repricing. The results remain statistically similar when we change the control group and when we estimate the model using firm and date fixed effects. This suggests that the findings are not driven by a specific comparison group or model specification and instead reflect gradual market reassessment of long-run office space demand relative to other property sectors.

title: Adapt to a Harsher World: Memo to the High Representative for Foreign and Security Policy
affiliations: Bruegel, Bruegel and Bruegel

detail.title: Adapt to a Harsher World: Memo to the High Representative for Foreign and Security Policy
detail.abstract:
The job of High Representative for Foreign and Security Policy and Vice-President of the European Commission (HRVP) was designed for a different world than the one the European Union now grapples with: a world built on principles and governed by law, in which the EU was a force of attraction because of its mass, prosperity and good governance. 

Today’s EU is weaker. It faces Russian aggression on its borders and a conflict in the Middle East where it has little influence. Economic security has become a much bigger priority. Whoever is elected as the next US president will continue the rivalry with China and be more absorbed with the Indo-Pacific than with Europe. In the EU, China is widely acknowledged to be a rival, and even a threat. Yet it remains an essential trade partner and has also become a formidable economic competitor. 

The HRVP’s role is constrained by a confusing and contested institutional structure, with prominent roles for the President of the Commission and President of the European Council in EU external representation. At the same time, the EU’s external policy is more important than ever. A stark choice must be made on how to adapt the HRVP role to a world dominated by intimidation and brute force. There are two possible options. 

The first and best option is for the European Council to give the HRVP a stronger mandate to act on matters on which member states have decided to take common action. This would require stronger legal and financial capabilities to coordinate relevant policies in the EU institutions. In this model, the HRVP would be ‘first among equals’, both among the foreign ministers and among all commissioners with portfolios that touch on EU external relations. 

A second option would be to accept that the authority of the HRVP is more circumscribed than envisaged by the Lisbon Treaty, but to clarify the functions that the HRVP will keep. This requires a clear division of labour with other commissioners whose portfolios have an external dimension and implies forsaking responsibility for trade policy, development, enlargement and neighbourhood, and even defence procurement. 

We believe the first model is preferable. But most important is that the EU makes a choice and breaks the bad habit of nominally assigning powers to the HRVP while depriving her of the ability to exercise them in practice. Disempowering the HRVP’s position would make the system even more dysfunctional.

detail.abstract: This paper re-evaluates the international macroeconomic trilemma by embedding segmented foreign exchange markets into a constant elasticity of substitution (CES) interest parity framework. Using a novel panel of implied parallel exchange rates, we analyze the transmission of U.S. monetary policy shocks across exchange rate and capital control regimes. Static estimates demonstrate that monetary autonomy is not merely a discrete policy choice, but is fundamentally conditioned on the elasticity of substitution between official and shadow markets. Dynamically, local projections reveal that parallel markets absorb external pressures when official channels are constrained, and expose stark asymmetric responses driven by a "fear of appreciation." Nominally flexible regimes with capital controls maintain autonomy during U.S. tightening but aggressively import U.S. rate cuts during easing, highlighting the practical limits of monetary independence.

detail.abstract: The Federal Reserve possesses multiple internally consistent inflation measures and systematically presents the public with whichever aggregation supports accommodation. Across five chairmanships and six inflation episodes (1973-2025), the committee operationalized dovish decomposition-arguments that measured inflation overstates true price pressure-as public frameworks, congressional testimony, and policy anchors. When the same analytical toolkit produced hawkish decompositions-arguments that measured inflation understates true pressure-the committee discussed the findings internally and declined to adopt them. Staff built three hawkish analytical frameworks (the Bubble Policy, asset-inclusive inflation indices, Market-Based PCE as binding target); all three were rejected. The two major preemptive tightening cycles in the post-Volcker era (1994 and 2015-2016) employed no compositional analysis at all, relying on Phillips Curve projections-while dovish decomposition ran in parallel. The asymmetry operates not through direction of individual claims, which run both ways, but through which claims become policy output. The mechanism is institutional preservation of discretion: the committee rejects any framework that constrains future options, and because the path of least resistance defaults to 1 Simpson's Paradox in Monetary Policy accommodation, preserving discretion produces accommodative bias as a downstream consequence. The choice of which inflation average to present publicly functions as a de facto policy instrument, operating parallel to the federal funds rate.

title: Unpacking China’s Industrial Policy and its Implications for Europe
affiliations: Bruegel and Bruegel

detail.title: Unpacking China’s Industrial Policy and its Implications for Europe
detail.abstract:
China is often credited with a successful application of industrial policy. One important particularity of China’s industrial policy is that it aims at levelling the playing field between the state economy and the private economy in access to finance, yet within a framework of strategic goals. This aim is not relevant for market economies, such as those of the European Union, but only for those where state enterprises are clearly privileged. 

Notwithstanding the difficulties in making valid comparisons, our analysis of how China conducts industrial policy in a variety of sectors points to success in some sectors but not all. More importantly, productivity growth in China has already been declining for two decades. 

Given the very large resources that China has put into industrial policy, with subsidies being only one part, it is surprising that success is not more evident. This relates partly to factors including cronyism and regional protectionism. While the former might be less relevant for the EU given the different institutional background, the latter certainly is relevant since the EU faces the potential consequences of member country-level industrial policy for its single market. A lesson from China seems to come from the sectoral focus, with a long-term and economic-security mindset. The EU is far from this, but it is in the process of linking economic security to industrial policy. 

Finally, responding to China’s industrial policy involves diverse investigations and challenges in measuring subsidies accurately. Understanding China’s very diverse and complex approach to helping companies achieve the government’s industrial policy goals is crucial for anticipating the consequences of China’s actions. These could be positive, such as cheaper imports of green technology, or negative, such as Chinese overcapacity spilling over to the EU single market.

detail.abstract: Can transparent order-flow environments discipline informed trading even in the absence of public enforcement? We study a DeFi market in which sandwich-capable MEV searchers impose immediate, state-dependent execution losses on aggressive informational trading. In a baseline equilibrium execution model, predation risk enters the trader’s problem through a predictable attack intensity and state-contingent jump/loss terms, generating an endoge nous shadow tax on aggressive trading and a safe-harbor region of near-zero execution. We then discipline these reduced-form objects through a bot-side partial-observation impulse control problem, which rationalizes how greater trading aggressiveness and detectability increase predation exposure. As a pricing extension, we show that the same predation channel can load equilibrium prices with additional jump-driven tail risk under a pro jected Cox representation and an LP-based pricing kernel. Our contribution shows that transparent DeFi microstructure can implement a private deterrence technology with real distributional and pricing consequences

title: Transparency of Carbon-Neutral Labels: Evidence from a Choice Experiment

detail.title: Transparency of Carbon-Neutral Labels: Evidence from a Choice Experiment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: I acknowledge financial support from Eawag: Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether transparency affects consumers’ willingness to pay for carbon-neutral labels. Many companies label products as carbon neutral, yet these labels do not disclose the shares of CO₂ offsetting and CO₂ reduction underlying the claim. The EU has recently adopted rules to prohibit environmental claims that rely on CO₂ offsetting, while other jurisdictions, such as the UK, have issued guidance recommending disclosure. Using a discrete choice experiment with 1,339 UK tea consumers, I compare willingness to pay for standard versus transparent carbon-neutral labels that disclose the offset–reduction composition. I find no evidence that transparency increases willingness to pay or that consumers prefer CO₂ reductions over offsets. Furthermore, organic and ethical trade labels crowd out the value of the carbon-neutral claim but do not change the null effect of transparency. These findings suggest that disclosure alone may not be sufficient to ensure quality differentiation in carbon-neutral labeling and that additional regulation may be needed.

title: Territorial Tensions: Rainforest Conservation, Post-Conflict Recovery, and Land Tenure in Liberia
affiliations: and

detail.title: Territorial Tensions: Rainforest Conservation, Post-Conflict Recovery, and Land Tenure in Liberia
detail.abstract:
Since the cessation of the civil conflict in 2003, the Liberian government is poised to 
expand greatly its protected area network to conserve the country's remaining rainforest. Liberia 
holds within its borders nearly half of the remaining Guinean rainforest, a global biodiversity 
hotspot. The planning process for this effort has been a central part of rebuilding Liberia's 
forestry sector, which helped fuel past conflict. The process, known as the Liberia Forestry 
Initiative (LFI), is widely considered to have been exemplary with regard to multi-stakeholder 
dialogue and policy making. Because the issue of land tenure remains widely contested however, 
the initiative risks seriously aggravating land rights problems, complicating the prospects for a 
durable peace. This article focuses on the process through which land was zoned for strict 
protection and how this process is likely to exacerbate land tenure conflict in Liberia’s priority 
conservation areas. Although the international conservation community sees post-conflict 
scenarios as opportune for promoting conservation initiatives, unresolved land tenure issues 
make for problematic outcomes, including land disputes and legal disarray. Such problems can 
result in significant volatility, and can make the peace process and recovery much more, not less 
difficult. Key Words: Postwar, Liberia, forests, tenure, conservation

title: Linkages Between Large-Scale Infrastructure Development and Conflict Dynamics in East Africa

detail.title: Linkages Between Large-Scale Infrastructure Development and Conflict Dynamics in East Africa
detail.abstract: With the rapid increase in the number of mega-infrastructure projects underway across East Africa, understanding how the social, economic, political and environmental repercussions of these projects intersect with ongoing conflict dynamics, is a poorly understood topic. Although recent interest in large-scale land acquisitions has led to a number of detailed investigations into specific projects and trends, there has not yet been a broad, systematic review of how large-scale infrastructure developments in East Africa interact with previous, ongoing and potential conflict in their areas of operation. The objective of this article is to report on an analysis of 26 megainfrastructure projects across Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Uganda, with an explicit focus on the common tension points that contribute to security dynamics. The methodology used involved two composite indicators of risk-a conflict risk score, and a project impact score. The study found seven common tensions across all projects: in-migration, population displacement and relocation, a negative history of community relations with previous or follow-on developments, 4) land rights, securitization, environmental degradation, and expectations of the local population relative to benefits delivered by the project. The study recommends increased attention on prior assessments that focus on the broader and more interconnected impacts in addition to those confined to the immediate project location, as well as in-depth examination of possible mitigation measures. title: Pricing Protection: Credit Scores, Disaster Risk, and Home Insurance Affordability
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, The Wharton School - University of Pennsylvania, Real Estate Department, University of Wisconsin-Madison and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Pricing Protection: Credit Scores, Disaster Risk, and Home Insurance Affordability
detail.abstract:
We use 70 million policies linked to mortgages and property-level disaster risk to show that credit scores impact homeowners insurance premiums as much as disaster risk. Homeowners with low credit pay 24% more for identical coverage than high–credit score homeowners. Leveraging a natural experiment in Washington State, we find that banning the use of credit information considerably weakens the relationship between credit score and pricing. We discuss the role of credit information in pricing and show that, although insurance is often overlooked in discussions of home affordability, a low credit score increases premiums roughly as much as it raises mortgage rates.

title: Environmental Change and Adaptation in Degraded Agro-Ecosystems: The Case of Highland Madagascar
affiliations: , Indiana University and Indiana University

detail.title: Environmental Change and Adaptation in Degraded Agro-Ecosystems: The Case of Highland Madagascar
detail.abstract: While the view that the poorer agricultural populations in developing countries will be at the forefront of negative consequences due to environmental change is widely accepted, this perspective must become considerably more nuanced in order to recognize and take advantage of emerging opportunities for realistic adaptation. This paper presents a case from Madagascar which suggests that adaptation opportunities involve more than looking for alternatives to what are presently perceived to be negative socio-ecologic processes. In Madagascar the severe erosion occurring on the deforested central plateau actually appear to create, over time, opportunities for increased food security and environmental management compared to un-eroded portions of the same landscape. The paper proposes that while concern and action is needed to attend to the problems that the poor of the developing world will face due to impacts from environmental change, the repercussions of such change on agricultural systems also need to be looked at in ways that involve recognizing the local and aggregate potential opportunities that they may present in certain systems, in order to realize the prospects for adaptation.

title: From the Administrative Presidency to Personalist Consolidation: Trumpism and Executive Control of the Regulatory State

detail.title: From the Administrative Presidency to Personalist Consolidation: Trumpism and Executive Control of the Regulatory State
detail.abstract: This essay investigates the evolving relationship between Trumpism and the United States regulatory state, focusing on how Donald Trump has reshaped American administrative governance to one of personalist consolidation. Drawing on scholarship of the administrative presidency, I argue that Trumpism represents a strategic fusion of structural deregulation in sectors like environmental protection, energy, and finance with robust state intervention in domains tied to a right-wing populist definition of national sovereignty. Trumpism reflects a personalist style of governance rooted in the exploitation of institutional tools of the administrative presidency that have developed across both Democratic and Republican administrations over the past century. By situating Trump within the broader institutional evolution of executive power, I highlight how his manipulation of the regulatory state entrenches executive dominance and preserves an illiberal reform in governance through electoral legitimation paired with the erosion of liberal-democratic accountability standards in administration (Bauer & Becker, 2020; Bauer et al., 2021; Bauer, 2025).

title: Position Auctions with Organic Search
affiliations: and

detail.title: Position Auctions with Organic Search
detail.abstract: Recent regulatory actions, such as the FTC v. Amazon antitrust case, have raised concerns about the impact of sponsored advertisements on consumer welfare in online search platforms. While theoretical models of position auctions typically predict that sellers are ranked by consumer-match/seller-quality in equilibrium, these models often abstract from the coexistence of sponsored and organic listings. We develop a model in which sellers can appear in both sponsored and organic positions and examine how this affects equilibrium outcomes and consumer welfare. Our model captures a key tradeoff: high-quality sellers value the visibility from sponsored placement but also expect to appear prominently in organic rankings. As a result, under certain conditions, lower-quality sellers may outbid them to obtain the sponsored position-lending some support to the FTC's concern. However, we show that this outcome only arises when all sellers are relatively high-quality, which limits potential consumer harm.

title: The Relationship Between Indigenous Pastoralist Resource Tenure and State Tenure in Somalia

detail.title: The Relationship Between Indigenous Pastoralist Resource Tenure and State Tenure in Somalia
detail.abstract: Indigenous resource tenure systems in Africa have evolved to meet the constraints and opportunities of often difficult biophysical environments, while facilitating the operation of complex spatial and temporal land use patterns. Traditional systems provide security of tenure in culturally relevant ways that permit adaptation to new circumstances. On the other hand imposed tenure structures in Africa have often not strengthened individual rights and have often blocked indigenous tenure development and adaptation in response to new situations. Pastoralists in Africa have in particular been negatively impacted by the imposition of national tenure systems which in many cases have served to marginalize nomadic populations, with repercussions in land degradation, food security, and instability. In Somalia the transient resource rights and resource use arrangements that are critical to transhumant pastoralism were ignored in the formulation of the national tenure regime which favored crop cultivation. The results were increased land degradation, resource use conflicts, declines in pastoral production, and impacts on Somali clan alliances which in many cases regulate rational resource access and use. Somalia posses the greatest proportion of pastoralists in Africa. Transhumant pastoralism, as the most widespread agricultural enterprise in the country, will play a critical role in food production for the foreseeable future. However the relationship between indigenous pastoralist tenure and state imposed tenure, has in many locations decreased the ability of pastoralism to reproduce itself, thereby compromising the rational utilization of very large areas of rangeland interior, which have very few alternative uses.

title: Learning-Based Portfolio Policies: Risk-Sensitive Control, Distributional Stability, and Representation Geometry

detail.title: Learning-Based Portfolio Policies: Risk-Sensitive Control, Distributional Stability, and Representation Geometry
detail.abstract: We develop a mathematical framework for learning-based portfolio policies in environments characterized by tail risk, distributional uncertainty, and high-capacity machine learning models. Rather than treating portfolio optimization as a static problem, we model learning systems as operators mapping observable information into predictive probability laws and study how portfolio policies act on these learned distributions. The analysis integrates risk-sensitive stochastic control, distributional stability, and representation geometry. We show that portfolio performance depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on stability of learned distributions and geometric properties of the representation manifold. In particular, distributional drift and curvature effects can induce nonlinear amplification of tail risk, leading to unstable policy behavior. The framework provides theoretical guidance for constructing robust learning-based portfolio policies and offers practical diagnostics for monitoring stability under regime shifts. The results position portfolio learning within a broader mathematical program linking stochastic control, optimal transport, and information geometry for robust financial decision-making. title: The Impact of Auction Timing on Bidding Behaviors: Evidence from the Chinese Land Market

detail.title: The Impact of Auction Timing on Bidding Behaviors: Evidence from the Chinese Land Market
detail.abstract: This study examines how changes in auction timing affect bidding behavior, using data from Chinese land market transactions. In 2021, a new policy mandated that 22 cities shift from sequential to simultaneous auctions for residential land. Using an event study approach, I find simultaneous auctions lead to higher prices and a greater auction failure rate. Additionally, I examine testable implications related to the mechanism behind the policy effect: auction prices rise more for higher-quality land and in cities with higher land quality variance; moreover, the auction failure rate increases more for lower-quality land. I then developed a model of bidding that rationalizes my main findings and offers some policy suggestions.
